main_body: Thatched-roof hut: a large straw roof (rows 0-37) over a plank wall with a door, a shuttered window and a stone step (rows 38-63)
top_band: Golden thatch roof slope from row 0 to about row 35, lightest at the ridge (rows 0-3) and in the eave band (rows 33-35), with a dark eave shadow at rows 36-37
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the roof slope is a tall, clearly visible top surface made of stacked thatch courses. A lighter eave lip at rows 33-35 marks the front edge, and a dark shadow at rows 36-37 sits right under it. The wall below is a separate vertical face of about 26 rows. The door has a dark frame and iron straps, and the window has a dark inner edge and shutters, so they read as inset. This is the same structure as the reference houses, where the roof slope is the top surface above the wall. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 steps from pale straw highlight through gold, mid, brown and dark, with course lines and per-bundle highlights, which is comparable to the reference roof tiles. The plank wall and door carry grain stripes, and the dark metal straps, window and stone step add variety. The outer silhouette of the roof is near-black, while the interior outlines on the wall and door are dark brown, hence mixed. Some thatch courses and wall planks are fairly uniform, so density is slightly below the reference. Nothing is a large flat fill, and it would sit acceptably beside the reference.
